description: High Resolution LiDAR Point Cloud data for AI-Integrated Infrastructure Damage Detection in Arctic Road and Bridge Condition Assessment, Disaster Creek, Alaska, 2024. is a data set deposited in UC Santa Barbara by its authors Emmanuel Chukwuemeka, Timothy Pasch (Research Institute for Autonomous System, University of North Dakota). Remote sensing makes it possible to gather data rapidly, accurately, and non-destructively, allowing for access to remote areas in near real-time. LiDAR sensor data were collected along Alaska's Dalton Highway as part of continued efforts to provide more geospatial data in Arctic regions relevant to cold region research. Coverage: a single site or case study; the metadata date the deposit to 2024. Formats: XML. It is reached through its DOI or landing page, listed on this page. Access is free of charge and open according to the repository. The licence is not stated (no licence in the DataCite metadata read on 2026-09-29). Caveats: written from the DataCite metadata (title, abstract, subjects and rights) read on 2026-09-29; the deposit itself was not opened or downloaded, so its contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support multi-sector infrastructure risk and planning studies. Related records: none catalogued yet for this repository.
